previous_description: A non-routable UI fragment embedded within a parent View. Two usage modes: (1) Library instance — 'ref' is populated with a ux.librarysubview specNodeId, rendering that reusable fragment; (2) Inline definition — 'ref' is absent and the SubView defines its own composition inline. SubViews are not independently routable; use View for routable pages.
definition: A non-routable region of a parent View that groups several component instances and is rendered only as part of that View. It is either a placement of a reusable LibrarySubView (ref set) or a one-off composition defined inline (ref absent).

distinguish_from.when: the fragment has its own route or URL, or is opened independently as a page, modal, dialog or drawer.
you are modelling the reusable fragment definition exported from a UX library, not its placement inside a particular View.
the element is a single configured library component with props, not a grouping of several components.
the element only declares which component fills a named slot of a parent component, rather than being a rendered region of a View.

standard_reference: HTML 5.3 §4.3 Sections (section/aside elements as sectioning content within a document)
code_evidence: A component file under a page's local folder (e.g. pages/Orders/components/OrderFiltersPanel.tsx) that is imported and rendered only by that route-level page and has no route registration of its own.
A template partial or include inside a page template, e.g. {% include 'orders/_summary.html' %}, @Html.Partial("_Summary"), or <ng-container *ngTemplateOutlet="summary">.

A named section of a page's render tree, e.g. <SidebarSection/> or a renderSidebar() helper, that composes several library components such as Table, Button and Input. A shared-fragment import from a design-system package indicates the library-instance mode.

attribute_descriptions.name: title
attribute_descriptions.description: Human-readable heading or name of the fragment as shown to users or designers (e.g. 'Order Filters'). Set it when the region has a visible heading or a recognisable name in design artifacts.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of what the fragment displays and what it is for within its parent View. Set it when the title alone does not make the region's content or behaviour clear.

notes: Inline mode lacks a 'components' attribute (LibrarySubView has one), so the inline composition is only expressible via relationships. Several relationships duplicate each other: aggregates/renders componentinstance; ref, realizes and uses librarysubview; view aggregates/composes subview. accesses data-store.collection and realizes business.businessprocess bypass the application layer and look misplaced.
